flawed_step: Step 0016: the prefix σ[..i] need not be a bad prefix. Although falsifying F(P1C ∨ P2C) at i means the original infinite word has no later P1C or P2C, that absence is not fixed by the finite prefix; an extension can introduce P1C or P2C later.
counterexample: Let Ξ={P1E,P2E,P1C,P2C}. Define σ(0)={P1E,P2E} and σ(k)=∅ for every k≥1. Then σ violates the property at i=0: the antecedent is true at time 0, while P1C∨P2C never occurs. The proposed prefix is σ[..0]=[{P1E,P2E}]. Now define an extension σ′ by σ′(0)={P1E,P2E}, σ′(1)={P1C}, and σ′(k)=∅ for k≥2. It has the same proposed prefix, but at time 0, F(P1C∨P2C) is true because P1C occurs at time 1. Moreover, σ′ satisfies the entire G formula: at time 0 the consequent is true, and at every later time P1E∧P2E is false. Thus the alleged bad prefix has a satisfying extension.
assessment_summary: The first definitive failure is in step 0016. A pending eventuality cannot be permanently falsified by any finite prefix, because a suitable event may occur in a later extension. The safety argument therefore fails.
